/boston/mattress/.name: How to Get Rid of a Mattress in Boston (City Pickup Rules)
/boston/mattress/.description: How to get rid of a mattress in Boston, using the City of Boston's own rules: mattresses can't go in regular trash, how to book the City's curbside mattress pickup (6 units or fewer), what to do in buildings with 7+ units, donation options, and asking the seller to take the old one. Sources: boston.gov (checked 2026-10-21).
/boston/mattress/.caption: A 1-minute summary of this guide, with the City of Boston's rules (checked 2026-10-21). Narration is computer-generated.
transcript: How do you get rid of a mattress in Boston? Here's what the City says.
Mattresses and box springs can't go in regular trash. Massachusetts bans them from disposal.
Building with six units or fewer? Book the City's curbside pickup. It's by appointment only, online at boston dot gov, or call 311.

Put it at the curb by 6 a.m. on pickup day, or after 5 p.m. the night before. If it's soiled or has bed bugs, bag and seal it completely. Don't cut or crush it. The limit is 10 items per address per calendar year.
Seven or more units? The City won't collect it. Ask your property manager, or use a hauler from the City's list.
Donating? Some furniture banks, like Furnishing Hope and Household Goods, take clean mattresses with no stains or rips. Many donation outlets don't take mattresses at all.
Buying a new one? The City suggests asking the seller to take the old one for recycling on delivery.
Every option, with official sources, is at bye bulky dot com. Rules change, so confirm before you haul.

transcript: How do you get rid of a mattress in Newton, Massachusetts? Here's what the City says.
Massachusetts banned mattresses and box springs from the trash in November 2022, so Newton won't take them as bulky waste.
Option one: pay sixty dollars per item online. If you pay by 10 p.m. Sunday, pickup should be set for Thursday of the following week. Set it out by 7 a.m.
Option two: drop it off at the Resource Recovery Center on Rumford Avenue for thirty-five dollars. Pay online first, bring proof, and unload it yourself. It's for Newton residents only.
Each mattress is one item, each box spring is another, and a split box spring counts as two. Futons and sleeper sofas go out as twenty dollar bulky items instead.

/boston/appliances/.caption: A 1-minute summary of this guide, with the City of Boston's and Mass Save's rules (checked 2026-10-27). Narration is computer-generated.
transcript: How do you get rid of an old fridge in Boston for free? There are two ways.
First, it can't go out with the trash. The City says Massachusetts law bans items with Freon from the trash.

Option one: book Boston's special item collection online or call 311. Put it where your trash goes by 6 a.m. on your day. The limit is five items per appointment and ten a year, and the City page doesn't mention a fee.
Take all the doors off, even on a mini fridge, and empty it. If the doors are on or there's food inside, it won't be collected.

Option two: if it still works and your electric company is a Mass Save sponsor, Mass Save picks it up at no cost and pays a seventy-five dollar rebate. It has to be plugged in, cooling, and ten to thirty cubic feet, and picked up in 2026.
